“Tadyathā | Mātṛ | Śubhamātṛ | Dharmamātṛ | Mātṛye nu sahitī ||” (Note:

Anuhrahma-tri avipratī-sara-tri ulukanā-matri vilukanā-matri muñcanugama-matri buddhe.
Ṣaṭṇāmatry anurokṣamatra dharmapratiṣṭhāna-matri mukṣamatri ananurudhavī.
Rudramatri ādamūmatri prahamabosthamatri jñālaṅkaramatri dhyānuśandikaruṇamatri dhyānuśandi muni.

Narmadā-niṣṭhāraṇa narmada sarvatrāṅgamana narmadā-jñapti-māra-haṃ hūṃ uṣṇīṣa-jaṭā-suta-vijayavati.
Pratipakṣasvabhāvasamādhi-niṣkrama mahā-vimāna-vyavalokaya jambudvīpa-kuruśrava-dharma-rukṣa-ma.
*Ṭiṃ kare me buddha-tiṣṭhānām.* At that time, the Great Brahmā King, Lord of the Sahā World, while residing in the Brahma realm,
heard this with his divine ear through the empowerment of this mantra of loving-kindness and the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha; having heard it, he immediately [assembled] with sixty-six...
Ten thousand Brahmā deities came to where the Buddha was, prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet, withdrew to sit to one side, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
By the power of the Buddha’s great kindness and great compassion, we shall protect this sutra.
If, in future ages, there are Dharma masters who receive, uphold, read, recite, transcribe, maintain, and make offerings to this profound and secret scripture;

and if those Dharma masters, whether in forest hermitages, on public roads, or in villages, towns, settlements, or royal cities, should proclaim such a sutra as this, we shall together provide them with protection and support, augment their vital strength so that they may be diligent, and cause their mindfulness, wisdom, and eloquence to increase in every respect.
"We shall cause those who lack faith to have faith, and we shall cause those who possess pure faith to abide in right practice.
World-Honored One!
We shall now together uphold the True Dharma-eye spoken by the Tathāgata and cause it to spread widely."
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Great Brahma King,
saying: “Excellent, excellent,
Brahma King!”
The Tathāgata now rejoices in your protection of the true Dharma.
Brahmā King!
Before long, you shall sit at the site of enlightenment and turn the wheel of the true Dharma, just as I do now.
"Just as you now protect this sutra, so too shall all other Brahmās in future ages protect and uphold the True Dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya, saying: "Maitreya!"
I now entrust to you this rare Dharma of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, which I have accumulated over immeasurable, incalculable, and koṭi-fold kalpas;
so that you may uphold, recite, and extensively explain it to others, thereby repaying the Buddha’s kindness and also fulfilling your own aspirations and vows.
To cause all sentient beings to increase their roots of goodness;
to cause all bodhisattvas to protect the light of the Dharma;
and to destroy all māras and non-Buddhists.
"It is for the sake of upholding the True Dharma and ensuring that the lineage of the Three Jewels is never severed.
Maitreya Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
I shall now constantly protect the treasury of the Dharma both while the Tathāgata remains in the world and after his parinirvāṇa. Why is this?
For I have also protected this True Dharma in the past.
"Bhagavān! Although I am in Tuṣita Heaven, I shall redouble my protection and preservation of such sūtras as these, so that they may long abide in the world. Bhagavān!"

If there are sentient beings in future ages who, having heard such sutras as these, receive and uphold them, copy them, read and recite them, practice according to the Dharma, and explain them extensively for others, you should know that all this is due to the empowerment of my majestic power.
World-Honored One!

At that time, even if there were Māras and their followers acting as a single faction, they would not be able to obstruct or hinder even a single hair of mine, which has been brought to fruition through roots of goodness divided into a hundredth part, a thousandth part, a *kalā* part, and even down to an *upaniṣad* part.

Even if every sentient being within the trichiliocosm were simultaneously a Māra or a follower of Māra, they could not create even a single obstacle to a fraction of the merit and wisdom derived from the roots of goodness I have accomplished; how much less could they obstruct the unsurpassed Dharma of Bodhi accumulated by the Tathāgata over immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* koṭi kalpas?
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Maitreya, saying:
“Excellent, excellent! O son of good family!”
There are four kinds of dharmas that constitute the practice of a bodhisattva. What are these four?
They are as follows:
To destroy the māra of afflictions;
to defeat all non-Buddhists;
and to bring sentient beings to maturity.
Upholding the true Dharma.
Good son, these four kinds are the practices of a bodhisattva.
These four types are subsumed within a single practice. What is this one?
It is as follows:
“Protect and uphold the True Dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Venerable Mahākāśyapa and the Elder Ānanda, saying:
“I entrust this sutra to you; you should receive and uphold it, and explain it extensively for others.”
Mahākāśyapa said: “World-Honored One!
I shall, according to my ability, diligently protect and uphold the Dharma of the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed enlightenment and proclaim it for others.”
Ānanda said: "So be it, World-Honored One!
I have received and upheld these essential teachings, and by the power of the Buddha, I shall widely proclaim and disseminate them in future ages so that they may never be interrupted."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Puṇyālaṃkāra rose from his seat, joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

This sutra, as taught by the Tathāgata, is profoundly deep and rare; it severs all webs of doubt and is the most supreme definitive meaning, difficult to see and difficult to realize. It accords with the emptiness of the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-śūnyatā*), is adorned with precepts, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom, and clearly proclaims liberation, tranquility, and non-defilement. It is the sphere of knowledge for all wise ones and is praised by all Buddhas.”

It is also the king of all sutras, sealed with the seal of dhāraṇī, which enables those who receive and uphold it to attain unimpeded eloquence, increase their mindfulness and wisdom, and remain firm and non-regressive;
it crushes demonic adversaries so that one cannot be destroyed by other heterodox schools;
and it can destroy evil precepts while increasing the merit of ascetic practices (dhūta) and non-attachment.
Furthermore, this is the merit of abiding correctly in great equanimity, which gives rise to the immeasurable wisdom-dharmas of all Buddhas.

If there are good sons or good daughters who can receive, uphold, read, recite, keep in mind, contemplate, and extensively explain this sutra to others; who copy it, make offerings to it, examine it with precision, attend to it according to principle, and act in accordance with right practice—how much merit will they obtain?
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Puṇyālaṃkāra in verse:
"With my Buddha-eye I behold the ten directions, The vast and boundless lands of all buddha-fields;
If they were filled to the brim with the seven treasures, And I were to give them all universally to all bodhisattvas;"
If a person upholds this sutra, as taught by the Buddha, with nothing to be attained,
and is able to practice its recitation and explain it to others, such merit shall surpass that [of the former].
With various flowers, fragrant ointments, and parasols, robes, silken fabrics, and banners and streamers,
filling and piling up throughout that world, they make offerings to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; and later,
in the final age when the Dharma is about to perish, if there should be those who receive and uphold this sutra,
If one practices as taught with heedfulness, the mass of merit obtained will surpass that [of the former].

Suppose the great oceans throughout the worlds of the ten directions were all filled with various kinds of oil, and wicks as tall as Mount Sumeru were lit to offer lamps at the *caityas* of the Buddha; [the merit of such an offering would still be surpassed by that of practicing with heedfulness].
If there be one who, at the time when that Dharma is perishing, when the world is entirely shrouded in darkness,
is able to kindle such a great Dharma-torch, the merit obtained shall be double that of the former.
If, for immeasurable guides, one serves them throughout billions of eons,
offering sublime celestial and pleasing provisions, and diligently seeks the most supreme Buddha-enlightenment.
To repay the profound and heavy kindness of the Tathāgata, One protects and sustains the Triple Gem so that it may endure for long;
To establish all sentient beings in the Buddha-dharma— The merit of upholding this sutra is greater than that.
Observing all sentient beings with the Buddha-eye, one may attain the rank of Brahmā or Śakra;
yet if there be anyone who can uphold this sutra, they shall obtain a most supreme merit that exceeds even those.
If one causes all sentient beings to attain arhatship, And further enables them to accomplish the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas;
Yet if there should be one who can resolve upon bodhicitta And uphold this sutra, their merit surpasses that of the former.
Even if the merit of these sutras were all transformed into form, it could not be contained within the entirety of space;
save for the World-Honored Buddha, the One of All-Knowledge, none can fully comprehend this supreme merit.
If, throughout billions of koṭis of kalpas, one were to uphold this sūtra spoken by the Tathāgata,
the merit produced would be immeasurable, as boundless as the ten directions.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Puṇyavyūha, having heard from the Buddha that the merit obtained from upholding this sutra is immeasurable, gave rise to great joy and leaped for boundless delight.
He addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
In the future, at the end of the age, if there are sentient beings who are unable to uphold this sutra, you should know that such persons have fallen into the realm of Māra."
“World-Honored One!
When I observe the roots of goodness obtained by protecting and upholding other aspects of the True Dharma, they are like mustard seeds;
yet, if there is one who can protect this sutra-dharma, the merit they obtain is like the empty space of the ten directions—without end and beyond all analogy.”

"Bhagavān! I have now donned the armor of valor; I would rather sacrifice my own body and life to protect and uphold this sutra, not out of a desire for my own benefit, but solely seeking the peace and happiness of all sentient beings."

When this Dharma was being taught, through the power of the merit of the Bodhisattva Mahā-ākāśagarbha, there were immeasurable Ganges-sands of Buddha-fields in the ten directions; from the void, the Bodhisattva Mahā-ākāśagarbha and immeasurable Buddhas and assemblies of bodhisattvas rained down various kinds of flowers as an offering.
A voice arose in the air and spoke these words:
"Excellent, excellent! Great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha!"
You are thus able to perform such vast buddha-activities, even unto this sublime adornment of the essential Dharma of this great assembly;
you are also able to sustain and uphold the future sentient beings’ adornment of the True Dharma, ensuring that they do not lose their bodhicitta.
"In this sutra, one should receive, uphold, read, recite, copy, and explain it.

At that time, wishing to entrust this scripture, the World-Honored One immediately emitted a great radiance from his body through his supernormal powers, which illuminated immeasurable Buddha-fields in the ten directions, causing them all to tremble.
There were immeasurable, asaṃkhyeya sentient beings who resolved their minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi;
immeasurable sentient beings attained the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).
Furthermore, immeasurable sentient beings attained liberation of mind;
furthermore, immeasurable sentient beings attained the purity of the Dharma-eye;
furthermore, immeasurable sentient beings became free from all defilements of greed.

Furthermore, there were immeasurable sentient beings who, having obtained the superior causes for merit among humans and devas, were destined to behold the Buddha; the entire great assembly gave rise to sympathetic joy.

When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahā-ākāśagarbha, the Venerable Mahākāśyapa, the Venerable Ānanda, Mahābrahmā the Lord of the Sahā World, Śakra Devendra, the Four Great Kings, the assembly of bhikṣus, as well as the great bodhisattvas, devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and all others in the gathering, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly delighted, and they faithfully accepted and practiced it.
